cds.title: Florida International University Common Data Set 2025-2026 (PDF)

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs for the full 2026-27 year from the Common Data Set (G1). Tuition $6,168 in-state, $19,806 out-of-state/nonresident ($205.57 and $618.87 per credit hour); required fees $398; on-campus food and housing $13,852 (housing $8,930 + meal plan $4,922). Estimated expenses (G5, residents): books $1,350, transportation $2,946, other $3,474 (other costs shown = transportation + other). FIU's international cost page (not dated) lists 30 credits at $6,167.10 in-state and $18,566.10 out-of-state, with athletic, health, parking and Panther ID fees bringing the matriculation totals to $6,565.88 and $18,964.75. CDS H6 for nonresidents ticks both 'need-based aid is available' and 'aid is not available' (contradictory) but reports that 872 degree-seeking undergraduate nonresidents received institutional aid, average $5,837 (total $5,656,443).

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 entering class): 36,103 applied, 21,976 admitted (60.9%), 5,854 enrolled. The residency table (in-state / out-of-state / international) adds up to those totals; the C1 men + women applicant rows add to 36,113, ten more than the residency total, and the residency total is used here. International first-years: 6,487 applied, 2,189 admitted (33.7%), 227 enrolled, versus 80.2% admitted for in-state applicants (16,632 of 20,734) and 35.5% for out-of-state. No waitlist figures are filled in and no early-action counts are given (C21/C22: the early-action closing date is listed, the Fall 2024 counts are blank). The average GPA of 4.00 with 65% in the 4.0 band means FIU reports a weighted/recalculated GPA; 99% of enrollees had a GPA reported. Test submission is the share of enrolled first-years: 92% SAT, 8% ACT (C9). Undergraduate enrollment (46,249) and the nonresident count (3,551) are the 'Total Undergraduates' figures (they include non-degree-seeking students such as dual enrollment). Admissions standards also include minimum SAT/ACT subscores under the Florida Board of Governors college-readiness rule (C8F).
